subject: CuraMetrics DPA follow-up: dataflow classification, subprocessors, and evidence requests
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@curametrics.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@curametrics.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Initial DPA follow-up: PII classification + subprocessor evidence needed

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — CuraMetrics is excited about the latency and cost controls you demonstrated. Procurement and our privacy team did a first pass on the DPA and we have a few follow-ups before we can move to legal review. Can you confirm the following items and share any evidence artifacts?

1) Data classification: we need a short mapping of request/response fields to PII categories (PII / Sensitive PII / Non-PII). A small CSV or table is fine.
2) Dataflow diagram: a diagram that shows where raw request data and ephemeral KV cache are stored, replication regions, and which components are considered in-scope for data export.
3) Subprocessor roster: up-to-date list of subprocessors (name, country, processing role, and whether they have SOC2 attestations).
4) Cross-border transfers: Do you transfer any customer-derived identifiers outside the US? If so, what safeguards/standard contractual clauses apply?

We appreciate anything you can provide this week — procurement has a Friday cadence. If it's helpful, we can schedule a 30-min sync with your privacy/infra folks.

Best,
Elena
Elena Park
Head of Privacy, CuraMetrics
Elena.Park@curametrics.com

Subject: Re: Initial DPA follow-up: PII classification + subprocessor evidence needed

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (privacy ops) and Rishi (infra) to provide the artifacts; below is a short plan and what we can attach now.

Quick answers up-front:
- Cross-border transfers: Redwood processes customer content in the US by default; customers can pin region(s). We do not export customer identifiers to third parties for analytics without contractual agreement. When transfers occur (e.g., for Dedicated cluster replication to EU region if customer pins to EU), we rely on SCCs and documented export controls.

Deliverables attached now:
- redwood-dataflow-diagram-v2.png — annotated diagram showing request ingress, routing, KV cache behavior, and storage scopes (ephemeral vs. persisted artifacts).
- subprocessor-roster-2026.csv — current roster with country and SOC2 status.
- dpa-annex-summary-2026.pdf — short annex that maps DPA clauses to runtime controls.

Notes and short mapping:
- Minimal PII mapping (below) — we will export a single CSV table matching your item #1 by EOD Thursday.

Field -> PII Category
- user_id (UUID) -> PII (identifier)
- user_email -> PII (contact)
- profile.name -> PII (contact)
- message_content -> Potentially PII (free text; classification depends on customer workload)
- model_output -> Non-PII by default (customer object), but could contain PII if original prompt contained it

Next steps: Marissa will follow up with the formal CSV and a short narrative about our retention tiers and access boundary. Rishi will add a short note on KV cache retention and how we encrypt keys at rest.

If you want an expedited call, Marissa is available Thursday 15:00–16:30 ET.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-dataflow-diagram-v2.png (png), subprocessor-roster-2026.csv (csv), dpa-annex-summary-2026.pdf (pdf)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@curametrics.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 14:18:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA follow-up: PII classification + subprocessor evidence needed

Hi Elena — following up with the promised CSV and a few clarifying details.

Please find the short CSV (pasted below) and clarifications on access and retention. If you prefer the file attached in a secure SharePoint folder we can push it there and send a link.

--- CSV snippet (Field,Category,Notes) ---
user_id,PII,UUID used for routing and access controls; pseudonymizable by customer request
user_email,PII,Used for notifications; hashed in telemetry exports where possible
profile.name,PII,Stored in user profile store linked to account id
message_content,Potentially PII,Ephemeral during inference; persisted only if customer enables training/retention
model_output,Non-PII,Considered customer data; no profiling done on our side unless customer opts in

Access & retention notes:
- Ephemeral KV cache: retained in-memory for up to 60 minutes by default; encrypted in memory and not written to disk unless explicitly configured for persistence.
- Persisted artifacts: logs and telemetry that contain identifiers are redacted or hashed in exports; full unredacted logs are available only for support cases with customer consent and are time-limited (14 days snapshot by default, longer for Dedicated customers under contract).
- Subprocessor SOC2: the roster indicates SOC2 Type II for core GPU hosting providers and our observability vendor; smaller tooling vendors may be Type I or undergoing audits (see CSV).

Attachments: we can drop the full CSV and a short access-control table into the SharePoint link Kimberly provided.

Let me know if you need a short statement for your procurement packet confirming we will not use customer identifiers for bench-marking without prior written approval. We can provide that as a one-paragraph attestation.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Privacy Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
